notes: Twenty-seventh daf of the campaign, second of the sixth five-daf checkpoint block. Fresh reconstruction of all 45 raw Rashi lines against the 11-id local segment table (l01, l05, l07, l10, l11, l14, l18, l21, l23, l24, l30). Drift profile ALIGNED, max offset 0, 0 semantic-audit shift candidates. This daf surfaced a genuine tooling defect (not a translation defect) in audit_rashi_semantic.py's anchors_of() citation scanner: raw line 27 opens a citation to Ezekiel that genuinely closes with its chapter number on raw line 28 (a real split across the Vilna print-line boundary), and the scanner's citation-closing lookahead (which appends the next line's first 40 characters to find such splits) also incidentally swept in a wholly separate, self-contained Psalms 77 citation that happens to sit within that lookahead window on raw line 28, misattributing it as a spurious duplicate anchor on line 27 and flagging a false shift-candidate that blocked the worker_pipeline.py review gate (drift-profile-ALIGNED and semantic-audit-zero-shift-candidates both failed, directing escalation to Fable). Since Fable is retired and the fix required touching a validator script outside the content-PR's allowed scope, this was escalated to the user per the campaign's own 'validator or workflow modification' escalation trigger; the user authorized fixing the tool in a separate PR. That fix (PR #175, merged to main at c1c7397, scripts/audit_rashi_semantic.py: skip a citation match whose entire span starts at or past len(he), since such a match never touched the current line) was verified against a fresh corpus-wide profile scan (21 pre-existing flagged daf, unchanged - no regressions) and the full drift-profile test suite before merging. With the fix merged, 28a now profiles as ALIGNED with 6 anchors (the spurious duplicate gone) and max offset 0, and rashi_verify.py --full now reports 0 shift candidates (previously 1 advisory). No attestation block is needed since the drift classification stayed ALIGNED throughout and never dropped to INSUFFICIENT-ANCHORS. Live-fetched Rashi_on_Yoma.28a from the Sefaria API; its LINE array omitted one genuine Rashi comment present in the raw print source (a textual/version note on raw lines 8-9 beginning 'does this mean a complete service requires a lottery... we do not read this', explaining that a certain repeated passage should not be included per the accepted girsa) - resolved by matching the comment's own opening words directly against the local segment table (its dibbur hamatchil 'lemeimra da'avoda tama' is l11's exact opening phrase) rather than relying on Sefaria's LINE grouping for that stretch, since Sefaria's specific edition apparently omits this particular editorial aside. Content covers: Rashi's own textual note explaining why the two 'but what of the limbs/fats, but what of terumat hadeshen' challenges from Rabbi Zeira's first formulation should not be re-read in this later formulation, since they were already covered (l01), the completion of Rav Asi's ruling that arranging two logs is a complete service since it finishes the wood-pile's own arranging (l05), the version-critical note declaring a stretch of intervening text (from the 'does a complete service need a lottery' challenge through the terumat hadeshen precedent) should not be read at all (l11 - a genuine Rashi comment absent from Sefaria's own LINE listing for this edition), the beraita proof that the two-log arranging is a complete service since a following limb-arranging exists, contrasted with the absence of any timed announcement for logs (implying it's a nighttime service and the true completion of wood-arranging, unlike limb-arranging which starts a wholly separate daytime service) (l18), the chapter-one-to-chapter-two transition heading itself (l23, reproduced plainly as structural text rather than commentary since it carries no dibbur hamatchil), and the second chapter's opening mishnah about the deputy High Priest's dawn-check ritual, the biblical citations proving night-invalidity and the barkai/brightness imagery (with the split Ezekiel/Psalms citation), the Hebron-visibility marker, the moonlight-mistaken-for-dawn incident and its consequence of removing the improperly-slaughtered offering, followed by the third mishnah about bringing the High Priest to immersion, the definitions of relieving oneself (cross-referenced to Nazir 54b and the Saul/cave verse from I Samuel 24), and hand/foot sanctification from the basin (l24, l30). The truncated single-word fragment on the final line ('gemara') is confirmed via modules/yoma/assets/talmuddev/28b.json's first raw Rashi line ('Gemara: he rose, more than daybreak...') to be the genuine truncated opening of Rashi's next comment continuing onto 28b, opening a fresh Gemara-section discussion; per the established boundary policy it is linked to 28a's own final local segment (l30) rather than invented as a phantom 28b id. Every raw-line English was checked against its byte-exact source line via direct dictionary lookup and a second full-file reread before finalizing, with explicit word-count majority decisions recorded at every boundary crossing.
